metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Transfer Pricing Compliance Platform domain: the annual documentation lifecycle Model -> Scope -> Collect -> Generate -> Localise -> File -> Monitor -> Defend as run by in-house tax teams, legal counsel, advisers and Reptune's own specialists on Reptune.net, plus the country content, service delivery and integration journeys that keep it running.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it, and lists the external systems (ERP and operational transfer pricing solutions, DocuSign, identity providers, tax authority portals, AI and machine translation providers, benchmark databases, corporate registers, regulatory sources, certified translators and e-mail) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Documentation Lifecycle Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a policy document and an entity list to filed, translated Master Files and Local Files: the journeys that set up the transfer pricing model, scope the year, collect and validate the numbers, generate the documentation and localise it for every country.

streams.name: Set up the transfer pricing model
streams.description: Take a multinational from a policy document, an entity list and last year's local files to a configured transfer pricing model in Reptune.net: legal entities and divisions, company types with their functional analyses, intercompany transactions with methods and benchmark placeholders, templates and custom text in the client's corporate identity. Configured once, the model drives every Master File, Local File and CbCR afterwards; with the R-AI onboarding assistant and Excel bulk entry a group is live in days, without installation, inside the free two-week trial.
outcomes: A new group with 5 to 500+ entities is modelled and generating a first draft Local File within days of signing up, not months
Company types, functional analyses and methods are defined once and reused by every entity, so documentation is consistent everywhere
The trial converts because the tax team sees its own entities, transactions and corporate identity in a generated report before buying

flows.title: Onboard a New Group in the Free Trial
flows.description: From the first login to a configured model: create the client organisation and users, bulk-load entities, define company types and functional analyses, register transactions and methods, style the templates and confirm the model with the R-AI onboarding assistant.
flows.trigger: A tax team starts the free two-week trial, or a new Core, Advanced or Enterprise subscription is activated and the kick-off call with Reptune customer success is scheduled.
flows.successSignal: The transfer pricing manager generates a draft Local File for a pilot entity in the group's own corporate identity and the model is marked ready for the annual cycle.

steps.title: Create the client organisation, divisions and first users
keyFacts: Every plan includes unlimited users, so the coordinator invites group tax, local controllers and advisers from day one instead of rationing licences.
Enterprise groups with several business units create divisions so each division sees only its own entities while group tax keeps the consolidated view.
painPoints: Groups that start with one shared login lose the audit trail of who changed what and have to re-invite everyone later.
Division boundaries that do not match the CbCR reporting group cause confusion once the first dashboard is opened.

steps.title: Bulk-load legal entities with the Excel template
keyFacts: The entity template is downloaded, filled from the group's entity list and uploaded in one go; validation flags missing countries, currencies and fiscal year ends before anything is saved.
Entities carry the attributes the generator needs later: jurisdiction, functional currency, ultimate parent, ownership and fiscal year.
painPoints: Entity lists kept by legal, tax and finance rarely agree, and the differences surface only when a Local File is scoped for an entity that finance does not recognise.
Retyping hundreds of entities screen by screen is the reason many onboardings stall in other tools.

steps.title: Define company types and functional analyses
keyFacts: A company type (for example limited-risk distributor, contract manufacturer, principal, shared service centre) bundles a functional analysis of functions, assets and risks that every assigned entity inherits.
AI-assisted writing drafts the functional analysis narrative from the type's characteristics, which the coordinator edits in place.
painPoints: Groups whose historical local files were written by different advisers have several descriptions of the same role, and choosing one becomes a political exercise.
Over-specific company types defeat the rule-based generator and end up as one type per entity.

steps.title: Register intercompany transactions and transfer pricing methods
keyFacts: Each transaction type (goods, services, royalties, financing) is registered with its transfer pricing method, tested party and the benchmark it will rely on, then linked to the entity pairs that transact.
The transaction register is what turns a Local File from prose into a rule-based document: every in-scope transaction of an entity is documented from the same definition.
painPoints: Transaction flows drawn on a whiteboard rarely match the intercompany balances in the ledger, and the mismatch is found by an auditor.
Methods chosen per adviser rather than per policy leave the group defending different approaches for the same transaction in different countries.

Report styling is configured once and applied to Master File and all Local Files, so the output looks like the group wrote it, not a tool.
painPoints: Tax directors reject reports that look generic even when the content is right.
Custom text pasted from old files carries stale facts that contradict the model.

The R-AI onboarding assistant answers 'what is still missing before I can generate' in the coordinator's language.
painPoints: Missing benchmarks and agreements are discovered at generation time instead of during setup.
Without a guided review the coordinator does not know whether the model is complete or merely populated.

Go-live needs no installation: the coordinator marks the model ready and the annual cycle can be scoped the same day.
painPoints: Pilot drafts reviewed in Word invite edits in the document instead of in the model, which the next generation overwrites.
Trials that end without a generated report are the ones that do not convert.

flows.title: Update the Model after a Restructuring
flows.description: A business restructuring, acquisition or policy change ripples through the model: new or retired entities and transactions, changed company types, updated custom text and adjusted access, all without touching the generated files.
flows.trigger: The group announces a restructuring, acquisition or a revised transfer pricing policy that takes effect in the next fiscal year.
flows.successSignal: The adviser confirms that all affected entities, transactions and functional analyses are updated in the model and the next generation reflects the new structure without manual edits.

steps.title: Identify affected entities, transactions and company types
keyFacts: The adviser lists which entities change role, which transaction flows start or stop and which company types need a new functional analysis.
Because the model is central, the impact analysis is a query, not a search through last year's files.
painPoints: Restructurings communicated late leave the documentation describing a structure that no longer exists.
Advisers working from memory miss the entity that quietly changed role.

steps.title: Revise company types and functional analyses
keyFacts: A new company type is added or an existing functional analysis is rewritten with AI assistance; entities are reassigned and the change is dated to the fiscal year it applies to.
Historical types are kept so prior-year files remain reproducible.
painPoints: Overwriting a type in place destroys the ability to regenerate last year's Local File for an audit.
Narratives written for the old structure survive as custom text and contradict the new type.

Validation checks that every new flow has a method and a tested party.
painPoints: Deleting transactions removes the evidence of prior-year documentation.
New flows without a method block generation later in the cycle.

streams.name: Scope and plan the annual documentation cycle
streams.description: Turn a fiscal year and an entity list into a documented plan: which entities need a Master File, a Local File, a CbCR or a notification under each country's thresholds, the automatically calculated deadline for each, the tasks and local contacts responsible, the e-mail reminders that keep them on track and the dashboard that shows the coordinator and the head of tax where the cycle stands.
outcomes: Every deadline for Master File, Local Files, CbCR and CbCR notifications is known and tracked from the first day of the cycle, so nothing is filed late
Scoping decisions per entity and country are recorded with the threshold that drove them, which makes the compliance position defensible
Local contacts know what is expected of them and by when, without the coordinator chasing by e-mail

flows.title: Scope the Fiscal Year and Calculate Deadlines
flows.description: The coordinator opens the new fiscal year, applies country thresholds to decide the documentation per entity, lets the platform calculate every deadline, assigns tasks and reminders and checks the resulting plan on the dashboard.
flows.trigger: The fiscal year closes and the group's entity list and preliminary revenue figures per entity are available.
flows.successSignal: Every in-scope entity has a documentation type, a calculated deadline, an assigned owner and a reminder schedule, and the dashboard shows the full cycle with no unscoped entities.

steps.title: Open the fiscal year and confirm the entity population
keyFacts: The new cycle starts from the Legal Module's time-stamped entity list as at fiscal year end, so entities acquired or liquidated during the year are handled correctly.
Divisions let group tax scope per business unit while keeping the consolidated cycle visible.
painPoints: Scoping from last year's list misses new entities until a local auditor asks for their file.
Entity lists exported from spreadsheets lose the 'as at' date that determines which year an entity belongs to.

steps.title: Apply country thresholds to decide documentation per entity
keyFacts: For each entity the country rule set states whether a Master File, Local File, simplified file, CbCR or notification is required, based on revenue, transaction volume or group size thresholds maintained for 170+ countries.
The coordinator confirms or overrides the suggested scope and records the reason, for example a voluntary file in a high-risk country.
painPoints: Thresholds change and groups that scoped from memory document too little in one country and too much in another.
Overrides without a recorded reason cannot be explained to the head of tax a year later.

dependencies.name: Documentation Scoping
dependencies.how: Records the documentation type per entity with the applied threshold and any override reason.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Supplies the current threshold and requirement rules per country.

steps.title: Calculate deadlines automatically for every scoped item
keyFacts: The deadline engine derives the Master File, Local File, CbCR and notification due dates per entity from the country rule, the fiscal year end and the tax return filing date where the deadline depends on it.
Deadlines are recalculated when the fiscal year end, the scope or the country rule changes, and the change is visible on the item.
painPoints: Deadlines maintained in a spreadsheet are copied from last year and silently wrong when a country moves from 'on request' to 'with the return'.
Different deadline bases (fiscal year end versus return date) are the classic source of a missed notification.

dependencies.name: Deadline Calculation Engine
dependencies.how: Calculates and recalculates due dates per scoped item.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Provides the deadline basis and offsets per country and document type.

steps.title: Assign tasks to local contacts, reviewers and advisers
keyFacts: Each scoped item becomes a chain of tasks (provide data, review draft, translate, file) assigned to the local controller, the coordinator or an adviser, with unlimited users so no one is left out for licence reasons.
Location-restricted profiles let a local contact work on their own entity without seeing the rest of the group.
painPoints: Task lists kept in e-mail threads are invisible to the head of tax and to a successor when the coordinator leaves.
Local contacts without access respond to data requests with spreadsheets of varying quality.

dependencies.name: Identity, SSO, User Profiles and Access Control
dependencies.how: Invites local contacts with location-restricted profiles.

steps.title: Set reminder schedules and communicate the plan
keyFacts: E-mail reminders go out ahead of each task due date and again when a task is overdue, so the coordinator manages exceptions rather than the calendar.
The plan is shared with the head of tax and advisers as a dashboard view rather than a spreadsheet snapshot.
painPoints: Reminders sent manually stop when the coordinator is on leave.
Plans shared as spreadsheets are out of date the day after they are sent.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Sends reminders before and after due dates.

dependencies.name: Compliance Dashboard and Worldmap
dependencies.how: Presents the cycle plan to stakeholders.

steps.title: Review the cycle plan on the dashboard and worldmap
steps.actor: Group Head of Tax / Transfer Pricing Director
keyFacts: The worldmap shows per country how many entities are in scope, what is due when and where a deadline is close; the head of tax signs off the plan from that view.
Unscoped entities and items without an owner are surfaced as exceptions before the cycle starts.
painPoints: Plans reviewed only as lists hide the concentration of deadlines in a few countries.
Sign-off without an exception list leaves gaps that surface in the audit committee.

dependencies.name: Compliance Dashboard and Worldmap
dependencies.how: Visualises scope, deadlines and exceptions per country.

dependencies.name: Documentation Scoping

flows.title: Re-plan when Scope or Deadlines Change Mid-cycle
flows.description: A new entity, a threshold crossed, a regulation update or a slipping task changes the plan mid-year; the platform recalculates, reassigns and escalates so the cycle stays on track and closes cleanly into next year's plan.
flows.trigger: A local contact flags a change (new entity, crossed threshold, changed fiscal year end) or a country regulation update shifts a deadline.
flows.successSignal: All affected items carry the new scope and deadline, tasks are reassigned, overdue items are escalated and resolved, and the closed cycle rolls forward into the next year's scoping.

steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The local controller reports a new entity, a merger, a crossed threshold or a changed fiscal year end through a task rather than an e-mail, so the change is attached to the cycle.
The coordinator sees the flagged change with its effect on scope before acting.
painPoints: Changes reported by e-mail are lost between the many threads of a busy cycle.
Local contacts unsure whether a change matters do not report it at all.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders

steps.title: Apply a regulation update to affected deadlines
keyFacts: When the country regulations specialists publish an updated rule, the deadline engine recalculates the affected items and lists them for the coordinator with old and new dates.
Content changes (a new required section) are shown alongside so the coordinator can add a task for it.
painPoints: Regulation changes learned from a newsletter are applied to some entities and forgotten for others.
Deadline changes without a change log leave the team arguing about which date was right.

steps.title: Reassign and escalate overdue tasks
keyFacts: Overdue tasks are reassigned when a local contact leaves or is unresponsive, and escalated to the head of tax when a deadline is at risk.
Dashboard filters show at-risk items per country so escalation is targeted.
painPoints: Escalation by e-mail arrives too late to save the deadline.
Reassignment without history loses what the previous owner already collected.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders

dependencies.name: Compliance Dashboard and Worldmap

steps.title: Confirm the revised plan with the head of tax
steps.actor: Group Head of Tax / Transfer Pricing Director
keyFacts: The head of tax reviews the revised plan and the list of changes since sign-off, and accepts risks explicitly where a deadline cannot be met.
Accepted risks are recorded against the item so the audit committee report reflects them.
painPoints: Revised plans presented without a change list get re-litigated from scratch.
Risks accepted verbally are forgotten when the audit letter arrives.

keyFacts: When the last item is filed, the cycle is closed and next year's scoping is pre-populated from it, with entities, owners and overrides carried forward for review.
The closed cycle remains the record of what was scoped, decided and delivered for the year.
painPoints: Cycles that are never formally closed leave the dashboard cluttered with stale items.
Rebuilding the plan from zero each year repeats last year's scoping mistakes.

streams.name: Collect and validate financial and transactional data
streams.description: Get the numbers that make a Local File defensible into the model with minimal effort from local finance: entity financials, segmented P&L per activity and transactional amounts per intercompany flow, entered through prefilled Excel templates or pulled directly from the ERP and operational transfer pricing solutions, validated on upload and cleared on the Actions Required page before generation.
outcomes: Local controllers submit validated data in one pass, because the template is prefilled with their entity's transactions and validation runs before the coordinator sees it
Segmented results per activity are available for every tested entity, so benchmark comparisons and Local File financials come from the same source
Data issues are resolved on the Actions Required page before generation rather than discovered in a draft

flows.title: Collect Entity Data through Excel Templates
flows.description: The local controller receives a data request, downloads a prefilled Excel template for their entity, fills in financials and transaction amounts, segments the P&L, uploads, resolves validation findings and confirms the data set.
flows.primaryActor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
flows.trigger: The data collection task for the entity becomes due and the local controller receives the e-mail reminder with the link to the template.
flows.successSignal: The entity's financials, segmented P&L and transactional data are uploaded, all Actions Required for the entity are cleared and the data set is confirmed and locked for generation.

steps.title: Receive the data request task and open the entity workspace
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The task states exactly which fiscal year, entity and data blocks are needed and links to the entity's workspace, where last year's submission is visible for reference.
Location-restricted access means the controller sees only their own entity and its transactions.
painPoints: Data requests sent as generic e-mails with attached blank spreadsheets are answered late and incompletely.
Controllers who cannot see last year's numbers reinvent the segmentation every year.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Delivers the request with due date, scope and link to the entity workspace.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Transactions Register
dependencies.how: Shows the entity's in-scope transactions the data must cover.

steps.title: Download the prefilled Excel template
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The template is generated per entity with its registered transactions, counterparties, currencies and prior-year values already in place, leaving only the current-year amounts to fill.
Advanced and Enterprise groups can use a custom transactional data model so the template matches their own data structure.
painPoints: Generic templates force the controller to interpret which line each intercompany flow belongs to.
Templates that do not match the ERP's data structure lead to manual re-keying and errors.

dependencies.name: Excel Templates, Bulk Upload and Data Validation
dependencies.how: Produces the prefilled Excel template for the entity.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Transactions Register
dependencies.how: Provides the registered transactions that prefill the template.

steps.title: Fill in entity financials and transaction amounts
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The controller enters the statutory P&L and balance sheet, then the amount per intercompany transaction from the ledger, in the entity's functional currency.
Mass upload handles entities with hundreds of transaction lines in one file.
painPoints: Intercompany amounts from the ledger do not reconcile with the counterparty's records and the difference is only found in a benchmark comparison.
Controllers entering amounts in the wrong currency create out-of-range results that look like a transfer pricing problem.

dependencies.name: Excel Templates, Bulk Upload and Data Validation
dependencies.how: Captures financials and transaction amounts from the filled template.

dependencies.name: Segmented Financials and P&L Segmentation
dependencies.how: Stores the entity's P&L and balance sheet for the fiscal year.

steps.title: Segment the P&L per activity and tested transaction
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The P&L is split per activity (for example distribution, manufacturing, services) using allocation keys agreed in the model, so each tested transaction has its own operating result.
Segmentation rules are stored with the entity and reused every year, and operational transfer pricing feeds can supply the segmented result directly.
painPoints: Segmentation done ad hoc in a spreadsheet by a different controller each year produces incomparable results.
Allocation keys that are not documented are challenged first in an audit.

dependencies.name: Segmented Financials and P&L Segmentation
dependencies.how: Applies allocation keys and stores segmented results per activity.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Transactions Register
dependencies.how: Links each segment to the tested transaction and method.

steps.title: Upload the template and run validation
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: On upload the platform checks completeness, sign conventions, currency, reconciliation of transaction totals to the P&L and year-on-year outliers, and lists the findings per row.
The controller fixes findings in the template or in the workspace and re-uploads until the data set is clean.
painPoints: Without upload validation, the coordinator becomes the group's manual data checker.
Findings reported weeks later, when the draft is reviewed, hit the controller in the middle of another close.

dependencies.name: Excel Templates, Bulk Upload and Data Validation
dependencies.how: Runs the data validation rules and reports findings per row.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.description: Findings on the Actions Required page.
dependencies.how: Registers open findings as actions for the entity.

steps.title: Resolve the entity's Actions Required
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The Actions Required page lists every open item that would block generation for the entity: missing data, unreconciled totals, transactions without amounts, unexplained outliers.
Each action can be resolved, explained or escalated to the coordinator as a task.
painPoints: Blocking issues hidden in a validation log are ignored until generation fails.
Explanations given by e-mail are not attached to the data and have to be re-explained to the auditor.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Lists blocking items and records resolutions and explanations.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Turns an action the controller cannot resolve into a task for the coordinator.

steps.title: Confirm and lock the entity's data set
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: The controller confirms the data set; it is versioned and locked so the generated files are reproducible, and any later correction creates a new version with a reason.
The confirmation closes the data task and moves the entity to 'ready to generate' on the dashboard.
painPoints: Data changed after generation without a version leaves the file and the numbers out of sync.
Coordinators cannot tell 'submitted' from 'final' when the controller keeps re-sending spreadsheets.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail, Versioning and Archive
dependencies.how: Locks the confirmed data set and versions later corrections.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Closes the data task and updates the entity status.

flows.title: Load Data Directly from ERP and Operational Transfer Pricing
flows.description: For groups with a direct ERP or operational transfer pricing integration, entity financials and intercompany amounts arrive by scheduled extract, are mapped to the model, reconciled and segmented, and only exceptions reach a person.
flows.trigger: The fiscal year is closed in the ERP and the scheduled extract for the documentation cycle runs.
flows.successSignal: All integrated entities have reconciled financials and segmented results in the model, exceptions are cleared on the Actions Required page and the data sets are approved for generation.

steps.title: Map ERP accounts and intercompany flows to the model
keyFacts: Chart-of-accounts lines and intercompany partner codes are mapped once to the model's financial lines, transaction types and allocation keys, per entity or per ERP instance.
Operational transfer pricing solutions can deliver already segmented results, in which case the mapping targets segments rather than accounts.
painPoints: Groups with several ERP instances and charts of accounts underestimate the mapping effort.
Intercompany partner codes that do not match legal entities produce transactions with unknown counterparties.

dependencies.name: ERP and Operational Transfer Pricing Integrations
dependencies.how: Stores the mapping from ERP accounts and partner codes to model lines and entities.

dependencies.name: Segmented Financials and P&L Segmentation

steps.title: Run the scheduled extract and stage the data
keyFacts: The integration pulls entity financials and intercompany amounts for the fiscal year, stages them as an upload batch and applies the same validation rules as an Excel upload.
The Excel interface remains the fallback for entities outside the integrated ERP.
painPoints: Extracts run before the local close is final import numbers that change afterwards.
Integration failures that go unnoticed leave entities silently without data.

dependencies.name: ERP and Operational Transfer Pricing Integrations
dependencies.how: Executes the extract and stages the upload batch.

dependencies.name: Excel Templates, Bulk Upload and Data Validation

steps.title: Reconcile intercompany amounts between counterparties
keyFacts: Amounts reported by both sides of a transaction are compared; differences beyond a tolerance become Actions Required with both entities named.
Reconciliation across the whole group is possible only because every flow is registered once in the transaction register.
painPoints: Unreconciled intercompany flows are the auditor's easiest finding.
Chasing differences by e-mail between two controllers in different time zones takes weeks.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Transactions Register
dependencies.how: Holds the amounts reported by both counterparties per flow.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Raises differences beyond tolerance as Actions Required.

steps.title: Segment results and review outliers

keyFacts: Segmented results are computed from the mapped data and compared with the prior year; margins that move sharply are flagged for the local controller to explain.
Explanations are stored with the data and reused in the Local File narrative.
painPoints: Outliers noticed only in the benchmark comparison come too late for a year-end adjustment.
Explanations lost between years have to be reconstructed for the auditor.

dependencies.name: Segmented Financials and P&L Segmentation
dependencies.how: Computes segments and flags margin movements.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Requests explanations for flagged movements.

steps.title: Approve the integrated data sets for generation

The audit trail records the extract, the mapping version and the approver for every entity.
painPoints: Data approved without a mapping version cannot be reproduced when the mapping changes.
Bulk approval without exception review lets one bad extract through.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail, Versioning and Archive

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required

streams.name: Generate Master File and Local Files
streams.description: Produce the Master File and every Local File at the press of a button from the validated model: pick the standard, localised or custom template per country, let the generator insert the functional analyses, transactions, segmented financials, archived benchmarks and intercompany agreements, add custom text with AI assistance, generate drafts in the corporate identity, review, and generate the final versions that are archived for the audit.
outcomes: Local Files for all scoped entities are generated in a fraction of the traditional time, 50 to 75 percent faster and cheaper for the group
Every file is consistent with the model and with each other, because content comes from one source instead of copy-paste between documents
Final files are versioned and archived with the data and template version that produced them, so they can be reproduced years later in an audit

flows.title: Generate Local Files for All Scoped Entities
flows.description: From the Actions Required check through template selection, automatic insertion of benchmarks and agreements, custom text, draft generation and review to final generation and archiving.
flows.trigger: Data sets for the scoped entities are confirmed and the coordinator starts generation for the fiscal year.
flows.successSignal: Every scoped entity has a final Local File in the corporate identity, generated without manual changes to the exported file, and archived with its data and template versions.

steps.title: Clear Actions Required before generation
keyFacts: Generation is blocked per entity while the Actions Required page lists open items: missing functional analysis, transaction without a method, unconfirmed data, missing benchmark reference.
The coordinator works the list group-wide, sorted by deadline, rather than entity by entity.
painPoints: Tools that generate regardless produce files with empty sections that reviewers spot too late.
Without a group-wide list the coordinator discovers the same missing item in each entity separately.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Lists blocking items per entity and blocks generation until they are cleared.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Shows which entities are ready to generate.

steps.title: Select the template per country and entity
keyFacts: The best-practice OECD-aligned template is the default; localised templates (for example Italy) are applied where a country prescribes structure, and custom templates where the group has its own house style.
Template choice is remembered per country so next year's cycle starts from the same selection.
painPoints: Using the standard template in a country with a prescribed structure means the file is rejected on form, not substance.
Custom templates that drift from the standard lose the automatic section updates when regulations change.

dependencies.name: Templates, Report Styling and Custom Text
dependencies.how: Provides the template per country and stores the selection.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Binds each entity's generation to the selected template.

steps.title: Let the generator insert benchmarks and agreements
keyFacts: Archived benchmark studies and intercompany agreements linked to each transaction type are inserted automatically as sections or appendices, with the arm's-length range and the entity's result side by side.
Missing links show up as Actions Required rather than as blank appendices.
painPoints: Manually attaching the right benchmark to the right file is where inconsistencies between Local Files begin.
Agreements stored on a shared drive are attached in the wrong version.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Pulls benchmark and agreement content into the file per transaction.

dependencies.name: Benchmark Studies, Arm's-Length Ranges and Entity Comparison
dependencies.how: Supplies the study, range and entity comparison for insertion.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Agreement Repository
dependencies.how: Supplies the current signed agreement for each transaction.

steps.title: Add custom text with AI assistance
keyFacts: Entity-specific narrative (local market, restructuring in the year, explanation of an out-of-range result) is written in custom text fields with AI-assisted drafting and editing in any text field.
Custom text lives in the model, so it survives regeneration and is reused next year for review.
painPoints: Narrative typed into the Word output is lost at the next generation.
Explanations written in different tones by different controllers make the group's files read as if from different authors.

dependencies.name: AI-assisted Writing and Editing
dependencies.how: Drafts and polishes custom text inside the model's text fields.

dependencies.name: Templates, Report Styling and Custom Text
dependencies.how: Places custom text blocks in the template's designated sections.

steps.title: Generate drafts in the corporate identity
keyFacts: Drafts are generated in bulk for the selected entities, rendered in Word and PDF with the group's styling and watermarked as draft.
A draft is a full file, not a skeleton, so reviewers judge substance and layout together.
painPoints: Drafts that need manual formatting after export create a second document that diverges from the model.
Reviewing skeleton drafts postpones the real review to the final version.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Generates draft files for the selected entities.

dependencies.name: Document Rendering and Export
dependencies.how: Renders drafts with styling and draft watermark.

steps.title: Review drafts with local contacts and correct in the model
steps.actor: Local Finance Controller / Country Tax Contact
keyFacts: Local controllers and advisers review the draft for the local perspective; corrections are made in the model or custom text, never in the exported document, and the file is regenerated.
AI-assisted editing helps reviewers rephrase a section without touching the underlying data.
painPoints: Reviewers who edit the Word file create a version the platform does not know about.
Comments sent by e-mail cannot be traced to the model change that resolved them.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Regenerates the draft once the model is corrected.

dependencies.name: AI-assisted Writing and Editing
dependencies.how: Supports rewording of narrative sections during review.

steps.title: Generate final versions and archive them
keyFacts: Final files are generated without the draft watermark, versioned with the data set, template and model version that produced them and archived per entity and fiscal year.
The archive is the documentation record used when a tax authority requests the file, sometimes years later.
painPoints: Finals kept on a shared drive are overwritten or lost when people leave.
Files that cannot be tied to the data they were generated from are hard to defend.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Produces the final files for the entities.

dependencies.name: Document Rendering and Export
dependencies.how: Renders and exports final Word and PDF files.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail, Versioning and Archive
dependencies.how: Archives finals with data, template and model versions.

flows.title: Produce the Master File
flows.description: The group-level Master File is compiled from the model's organisational structure, business description, intangibles, financing and financial position sections, drafted with AI assistance, validated and generated as a final version that every Local File references.
flows.trigger: The group's consolidated financials and organisational information for the fiscal year are available and the Master File task becomes due.
flows.successSignal: The Master File is generated in final form, archived and available to be attached to or referenced by every Local File in the cycle.

steps.title: Compile group-level sections from the model
keyFacts: The Master File template maps to the OECD Annex I structure; organisational structure, business overview, intangibles, intercompany financial activities and financial and tax positions are populated from the model and the current legal structure.
Transaction types and company types from the model become the description of the group's transfer pricing policies.
painPoints: Master Files written as a standalone narrative drift from the Local Files that are supposed to be consistent with them.
Group structure charts pasted as images are out of date by the time the file is filed.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Assembles the Master File sections from model content.

dependencies.name: Templates, Report Styling and Custom Text
dependencies.how: Provides the OECD-aligned Master File structure and styling.

steps.title: Draft group narratives with AI assistance
keyFacts: Business overview, value drivers, supply chain and intangibles narratives are drafted in custom text fields with AI assistance, based on last year's text and the model's structure.
The same text blocks are reused in Local Files where a country requires a group description.
painPoints: Narratives rewritten from scratch each year introduce inconsistencies with prior filings.
Group descriptions written for investors do not serve a transfer pricing audience.

dependencies.name: AI-assisted Writing and Editing
dependencies.how: Drafts and edits group-level narratives.

dependencies.name: Templates, Report Styling and Custom Text
dependencies.how: Stores narratives for reuse in Master File and Local Files.

steps.title: Attach group-wide benchmarks and policy agreements
keyFacts: Group-wide benchmark studies and framework agreements (for example a group services agreement) are linked to the Master File so the same evidence appears in every Local File that refers to them.
The list of important agreements and APAs is drawn from the agreement repository.
painPoints: Framework agreements listed in the Master File but not attached to Local Files invite requests for documents nobody can find.
APAs and rulings maintained in a separate list are omitted from the file.

dependencies.name: Benchmark Studies, Arm's-Length Ranges and Entity Comparison
dependencies.how: Links group benchmark studies to the Master File.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Agreement Repository
dependencies.how: Provides the agreement list and documents for the Master File.

steps.title: Validate the Master File content
keyFacts: Validation checks that every required section has content, that the entity list matches the legal structure as at year end and that the financial position figures reconcile with the CbCR data where both exist.
Open items are listed as Actions Required for the Master File.
painPoints: A Master File that contradicts the CbCR is a red flag for tax authorities that receive both.
Missing sections are found by the first foreign tax inspector who reads the file.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Runs section and consistency checks and lists Actions Required.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Cross-checks the Master File with the model content used in Local Files.

steps.title: Generate the final Master File and archive it
keyFacts: The final Master File is generated in Word and PDF in the corporate identity, versioned and archived, and referenced from every Local File in the cycle.
Later corrections produce a new version with a change note so local filings can be updated where required.
painPoints: Different versions of the Master File filed in different countries are hard to explain.
Master Files without a version history cannot show what was known when.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Generates the final Master File.

dependencies.name: Document Rendering and Export
dependencies.how: Renders the Master File in Word and PDF.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail, Versioning and Archive
dependencies.how: Versions and archives the Master File with change notes.

streams.name: Localise and translate documentation
streams.description: Turn an English Local File into a locally compliant file: apply the country's content, format and language rules and localised template, machine-translate into one of 28 languages with transfer pricing glossaries, let the local contact review terminology, order a human-certified translation where a country requires it, complete local forms and procedures and store the filed version.
outcomes: Local Files meet local content, format and language requirements without a local adviser rewriting them
Machine translation with glossaries makes multi-language documentation the default rather than a budget decision
Certified translations and local forms are ordered and tracked inside the cycle, so the local filing is complete

flows.title: Localise and Machine-translate a Local File
flows.description: Check the country's requirements, apply the localised template, generate the English final, machine-translate with the transfer pricing glossary, review terminology locally and export the translated file.
flows.trigger: The English draft for an entity in a country with local content or language requirements is approved and the localisation task becomes due.
flows.successSignal: The entity has a translated, locally structured Local File exported and stored alongside the English version, with reviewed terminology and the country's format requirements met.

steps.title: Check the country's content, format and language requirements
keyFacts: The country record states whether the file must be in the local language, whether a certified translation is required, which sections or annexes are mandatory and in what format and timing the file is submitted.
The R-AI country expert mode will answer the same questions conversationally; today the record is the reference maintained by the specialists.
painPoints: Requirements learned from a local adviser's memory differ per adviser and per year.
Language requirements discovered at filing time leave no time for translation.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Provides content, format, language and certification requirements for the country.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Carries the localisation checklist derived from the requirements.

steps.title: Apply the localised template and local sections
keyFacts: Countries with prescribed structures use a localised template (Italy is a published example) that orders and names sections as the local rules require and adds mandatory local annexes.
Localised templates are maintained by the country content specialists and updated when the rule changes.
painPoints: A file with the right content in the wrong structure is treated as non-compliant in some countries.
Locally maintained template copies drift from the group's standard and lose updates.

dependencies.name: Templates, Report Styling and Custom Text
dependencies.how: Applies the country's localised template and local sections.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Determines which localised template and annexes apply.

keyFacts: The English file on the localised template is generated as the translation source; translating a generated final rather than a draft avoids retranslating after corrections.
The source version is frozen so the translation can be traced to it.
painPoints: Translating drafts leads to repeated translation cost when the draft changes.
Untraceable source versions make it impossible to tell which English text a translated file reflects.

dependencies.name: Master File and Local File Generator
dependencies.how: Generates the English file on the localised template as translation source.

dependencies.name: Document Rendering and Export
dependencies.how: Exports the frozen English source.

Group-specific glossary entries (entity names, product names, defined terms) are added once and reused for every file and year.
painPoints: Generic machine translation renders transfer pricing terms differently in every paragraph.
Human translation of every Local File is the largest avoidable cost in a multi-country cycle.

dependencies.name: Machine Translation and Glossaries

dependencies.name: Document Rendering and Export

The review is a task with a due date derived from the filing deadline.
painPoints: Local reviewers who correct in the document instead of the glossary repeat the same fixes every year.
Reviews without a deadline are done the day before filing.

dependencies.name: Machine Translation and Glossaries
dependencies.how: Captures reviewer corrections as glossary entries.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders

painPoints: Translated files kept only in local mailboxes cannot be produced by group tax when the audit comes.
Formats not accepted by the local authority cause a filing to bounce.

flows.successSignal: The certified translation and completed local forms are filed with the local tax authority before the deadline and the filed versions are stored in the platform.

steps.title: Identify certification and local form requirements

Requirements are surfaced on the entity's task list, not left to local memory.
painPoints: Certification requirements discovered late add weeks to the local timeline.
Local forms filled in from an old template are rejected.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders

The order, its status and the certified deliverable are tracked on the task.

painPoints: Forms filled in inconsistently with the Local File are an audit trigger.
Procedures that require a local signatory or a portal account are found out on the deadline day.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Provides the forms and procedural guidance for the country.

dependencies.name: Expert Support and Advisory Hours

Filed versions not stored centrally cannot be matched to what the authority received.

Country records that are not corrected from field experience slowly lose accuracy.

rootGroups.name: Reporting, Benchmarks and Insight Journeys
rootGroups.description: From CbCR data to filed XML and public XHTML, from transaction types to arm's-length ranges, and from dashboards to audit defence: the journeys that make the group's position reportable, supportable and visible.

streams.name: Prepare and file CbCR and notifications
streams.description: Take the group from CbCR data to filed reports: confirm the reporting entity and constituent entities, enter or bulk-upload the CbCR tables, clear the Actions Required, generate filing-ready XML and Excel, produce the EU Public CbCR in XHTML with inline XBRL from the same data, and prepare and track CbCR notifications with automatically calculated deadlines per country.
outcomes: The CbCR is filed on time in valid XML, and the EU Public CbCR is generated from the same data without a second collection
Every CbCR notification is prepared and filed before its country-specific deadline
CbCR data is consistent with the Master File and Local Files, so the three tiers do not contradict each other in an audit

flows.title: Prepare and File the OECD CbCR
flows.description: Confirm the reporting entity and constituent entities, enter or bulk-upload Table 1, 2 and 3 data, clear validation findings, generate the XML per the required schema and Excel for review, and file with the tax authority within the deadline.
flows.trigger: The group's consolidated fiscal year data per jurisdiction is available and the CbCR task becomes due.
flows.successSignal: A valid CbCR XML is filed with the ultimate parent's tax authority before the deadline, the Excel version is archived and the filing is recorded.

steps.title: Confirm the reporting entity and constituent entities
keyFacts: The reporting entity (ultimate parent or surrogate) and the constituent entities per jurisdiction, with their main business activities, are taken from the time-stamped legal entity list as at fiscal year end.
Entities added or disposed of during the year are handled by their effective dates.
painPoints: Constituent entity lists maintained separately from the legal entity register omit dormant or newly acquired entities.
Business activity codes assigned once and never revisited misdescribe entities that changed role.

dependencies.name: CbCR Data Management and XML Output
dependencies.description: Reporting entity and constituent entity setup.
dependencies.how: Defines the CbCR reporting group for the fiscal year.

dependencies.name: Legal Entity Management
dependencies.description: Entity list as at year end.
dependencies.how: Supplies constituent entities with jurisdiction and activity data.

steps.title: Enter or bulk-upload the CbCR tables
keyFacts: Table 1 (revenues, profit, taxes, capital, employees, tangible assets per jurisdiction), Table 2 (entities and activities) and Table 3 (additional information) are entered manually or uploaded in bulk from Excel.
The same data is the basis for Pillar Two transitional CbCR safe harbour analysis, so quality matters beyond the filing itself.
painPoints: Data aggregated by jurisdiction from many sources loses the reconciliation to the consolidated accounts.
Manual re-entry of a spreadsheet prepared by consolidation introduces transcription errors.

dependencies.name: CbCR Data Management and XML Output
dependencies.how: Stores Table 1, 2 and 3 data per jurisdiction and entity.

dependencies.name: Excel Templates, Bulk Upload and Data Validation
dependencies.how: Loads the tables from the Excel template and validates the rows.

steps.title: Clear the CbCR Actions Required
keyFacts: Automated validation checks schema constraints, jurisdiction totals against entity lists, sign conventions and plausibility, and lists every finding on the Actions Required page.
Findings are resolved before generation so the XML passes the authority's validator the first time.
painPoints: XML rejected by the authority's validator on the deadline day is a stressful way to find a data error.
Plausibility issues (a jurisdiction with employees but no revenue) attract questions from every receiving authority.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Lists validation findings and blocks generation until they are cleared.

dependencies.name: CbCR Data Management and XML Output
dependencies.how: Runs the CbCR validation rules on the data set.

steps.title: Generate filing-ready XML and the Excel version
keyFacts: The platform generates XML in the format the ultimate parent's tax authority requires and an Excel version for internal review and for advisers or authorities that ask for a readable copy.
Both outputs are versioned so a corrected filing can be traced to the data change.
painPoints: Authorities' XML variants differ, and a file that validated last year fails on a new schema version.
Reviewers cannot read XML, so a filing is approved without anyone checking the numbers.

dependencies.name: CbCR Data Management and XML Output
dependencies.how: Produces the CbCR XML for the required schema.

dependencies.name: Document Rendering and Export

steps.title: File the CbCR and record the filing
keyFacts: The XML is filed through the tax authority's portal; the filing date, reference and filed version are recorded in the platform and the deadline item is closed.
The filed version is the basis for the EU Public CbCR and for answering local authorities that receive the report through exchange.
painPoints: Filings done by an adviser without recording the reference are impossible to prove later.
Deadline items left open after filing make the dashboard cry wolf.

dependencies.name: CbCR Data Management and XML Output

Consistency across the three tiers is what tax authorities test first when they receive all of them.
painPoints: Inconsistent entity counts between CbCR and Master File are an easy audit finding.
Explanations kept outside the platform are unavailable when the question arrives two years later.

dependencies.name: CbCR Data Management and XML Output
dependencies.how: Compares CbCR figures and entities with documentation content.

streams.name: Benchmark intercompany transactions
streams.description: Give every transaction type an arm's-length range and every tested entity a comparison against it: define the search per transaction type and functional profile, commission or upload the benchmark study, record the range, compare each entity's segmented result against it, surface out-of-range entities on the dashboard, insert the evidence in the Local Files and refresh studies on a multi-year cycle.
outcomes: Every tested transaction type has a current benchmark study archived in the platform and inserted automatically in the Local Files that rely on it
Out-of-range entities are visible during the year, in time for a year-end adjustment rather than an audit
Benchmark refreshes and financial updates are planned and budgeted rather than triggered by an audit request

flows.title: Archive a Benchmark Study and Compare Entity Results
flows.description: Define the benchmark per transaction type and functional profile, commission or upload the study, record the arm's-length range, compare the segmented results of tested entities, flag out-of-range results and insert the evidence into Local Files.
flows.trigger: A transaction type in the model lacks a benchmark or its study is due for refresh, and the coordinator opens a benchmark task.
flows.successSignal: The study and its range are archived against the transaction type, every tested entity has a comparison result, exceptions are flagged on the dashboard and the evidence appears in the generated Local Files.

steps.title: Define the benchmark per transaction type and functional profile
keyFacts: The benchmark definition states the transaction type, tested party's company type, method and profit level indicator, and the regions and years it should cover, so one study can serve many entities.
Definitions derive from the model, which keeps benchmark coverage aligned with the transactions actually documented.
painPoints: Benchmarks commissioned per entity rather than per transaction type multiply cost and inconsistency.
Studies whose tested party profile does not match the company type are rejected by auditors.

dependencies.name: Transfer Pricing Model, Company Types and Functional Analyses

steps.title: Commission the study or upload an existing one
keyFacts: The study is commissioned through Reptune's benchmark offerings, an adviser or run in-house on a commercial database, and the report and comparable set are uploaded and archived.
Existing studies from prior advisers are uploaded with their year and coverage so they are reused rather than redone.
painPoints: Studies delivered as PDFs on a shared drive are not found when the Local File needs them.
Different advisers use different databases and rejection criteria, making studies incomparable.

dependencies.name: Benchmark Studies, Arm's-Length Ranges and Entity Comparison
dependencies.how: Stores the study report, comparable set and coverage.

dependencies.name: Expert Support and Advisory Hours

steps.title: Record the arm's-length range and its validity
keyFacts: The interquartile range, median, profit level indicator and the years the study is valid for (with planned financial updates) are recorded against the transaction type.
Validity drives the refresh plan and the warnings when a study is used past its intended life.
painPoints: Ranges copied by hand into each Local File diverge over time.
Studies used for too many years are challenged on age.

dependencies.name: Benchmark Studies, Arm's-Length Ranges and Entity Comparison
dependencies.how: Stores range statistics and validity per study.

dependencies.name: Intercompany Transactions Register

steps.title: Compare each entity's segmented result against the range
keyFacts: For every tested entity the platform compares the segmented actual result with the applicable range and states whether it is within, above or below.
Comparisons run as soon as data is confirmed, so they are available during the year for operational transfer pricing decisions.
painPoints: Comparisons done once a year in a spreadsheet are too late to correct.
Results compared against the wrong segment (whole-entity instead of tested activity) mislead.

Explanations are recorded against the comparison and reused in the Local File.
painPoints: Out-of-range results discovered by an auditor are much more expensive than those discovered by the group.
Explanations given verbally are lost.

A study replaced by a newer version updates all files at the next generation.
painPoints: Manually attached benchmarks are inconsistent between files and years.
Files that show the range but not the entity's position invite the auditor to compute it.

flows.successSignal: Every transaction type documented in the next cycle has a current or updated study linked, and affected Local Files are regenerated with the new ranges.

steps.title: Identify expiring and missing studies
keyFacts: The validity report lists studies past or near their validity, transaction types without a study and entities whose results rely on them.
Advisers use the report to plan refresh work for their client portfolio.
painPoints: Groups that do not track validity refresh everything at once, or nothing.
Missing studies are noticed when the Local File shows an empty benchmark section.

steps.title: Decide between financial update and full refresh
keyFacts: A financial update refreshes comparables' financials for the same set; a full refresh reruns the search. The decision is recorded with the study.
Reptune's benchmark offerings cover both at a known price.
painPoints: Full refreshes commissioned by habit cost several times a financial update.
Financial updates run for too many years are challenged in audits.

Links not updated leave some entities compared against the old range.

Risk indicators and out-of-range results are acted on before an audit rather than explained during one

painPoints: Status reports consolidated in a spreadsheet are out of date before they reach the CFO.

streams.name: Maintain country regulations and deadlines
streams.description: Keep the platform's knowledge of 170+ countries current: specialists monitor OECD, EU and national sources, update thresholds, content, format, language and deadline rules, adjust localised templates, validations, glossaries and R-AI's knowledge base, publish the change to affected clients and answer country-expert questions that R-AI cannot yet resolve.
outcomes: Every country rule set is current within a short lead time of the regulatory change, so scoping and deadlines are always based on the latest rules
Regulatory change becomes templates, validations and R-AI answers that users act on, not a newsletter they must interpret
Country-expert questions are answered consistently, and each answer improves the knowledge base

flows.title: Process a Regulatory Change into the Platform
flows.description: From monitoring a source to a published change: update the country record, the deadline rules, the localised template and validations, the R-AI knowledge base and glossary, then notify affected clients.
flows.trigger: A tax authority, the OECD or the EU publishes a change to transfer pricing documentation, CbCR or public CbCR rules, or a specialist spots a change in practice.
flows.successSignal: The country record, deadline rules, templates, validations, R-AI knowledge base and glossary reflect the change with an effective date, and affected clients see it in their scoping and deadlines.

steps.title: Monitor sources and log the change
keyFacts: Specialists monitor legislation, guidance, filing schemas and announcements for the countries they cover and log each change with source, effective date and affected rule types.
Changes are prioritised by the number of client entities in the country and the proximity of deadlines.
painPoints: Monitoring 170+ countries by reading newsletters misses changes in smaller jurisdictions.
Changes logged without an effective date are applied to the wrong fiscal year.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Records the regulatory change and its source.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Creates the work item for the specialist to process the change.

steps.title: Update thresholds, content, format and language rules
keyFacts: The country record's thresholds, required content, simplified-file options, format, language and certification rules are updated with an effective fiscal year, keeping the previous version for earlier years.
A second specialist reviews the change before it is published.
painPoints: Single-specialist updates without review introduce errors that reach every client in that country.
Overwriting rules loses the ability to explain last year's scoping.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Updates the rule set with effective dates and review.

dependencies.name: Documentation Scoping
dependencies.how: Shows which clients' scoped items are affected.

steps.title: Update deadline rules and recalculate
keyFacts: Deadline bases and offsets for Master File, Local File, CbCR and notification are updated; the engine recalculates affected deadlines in client cycles and logs old and new dates.
Deadline changes are among the most frequent and most consequential updates.
painPoints: A deadline rule updated without recalculation leaves clients with the old date.
Rules with several deadline bases (return date, year end, on request) are easy to encode wrongly.

dependencies.name: Deadline Calculation Engine
dependencies.how: Updates the rule and recalculates affected client deadlines.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Holds the updated deadline rule with its source.

steps.title: Update localised templates and validations
keyFacts: New required sections or annexes are added to the localised template and the validations that flag missing content, so clients see the requirement as an Actions Required item rather than a footnote.
Template changes are versioned per fiscal year.
painPoints: Requirements documented only in the country record are not enforced.
Template changes applied to prior years alter filed content.

dependencies.name: Templates, Report Styling and Custom Text
dependencies.how: Updates the country's template with a new version.

dependencies.name: Pre-generation Validation and Actions Required
dependencies.how: Adds or changes validations for the new requirement.

steps.title: Update the R-AI knowledge base and translation glossary
keyFacts: The change is written into the knowledge base R-AI uses for onboarding and country-expert answers, and new terms are added to the transfer pricing glossary for the country's language.
Answers are tested against the change before publication.
painPoints: An assistant that answers from stale content is worse than no assistant.
New regulatory terms translated inconsistently confuse local reviewers.

dependencies.name: R-AI Assistant (Onboarding and Country Expert)
dependencies.how: Publishes the change to R-AI's country knowledge.

dependencies.name: Machine Translation and Glossaries
dependencies.how: Adds terminology for the change in the local language.

steps.title: Publish the change and notify affected clients
keyFacts: The change is published with its effective date; coordinators of affected clients receive a notification with the impact on their scope and deadlines.
Publication is logged as evidence of the platform's regulation update lead time.
painPoints: Changes published silently are discovered by clients as unexplained deadline shifts.
Notifications sent to everyone are ignored; targeted ones are read.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Publishes the updated rule set.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Notifies affected coordinators with the impact summary.

dependencies.name: Documentation Scoping
dependencies.how: Determines which clients and entities are affected.

flows.title: Answer a Country-expert Question
flows.description: A user asks R-AI about a country's requirements; unresolved questions are escalated to a specialist whose answer enriches the knowledge base, and coverage is reviewed periodically.
flows.trigger: A coordinator, controller or adviser has a question about a country's documentation requirement, deadline or procedure.
flows.successSignal: The question is answered consistently with the country record, the answer is captured in the knowledge base and the query resolution is tracked.

steps.title: Ask R-AI in any language
keyFacts: R-AI answers product and onboarding questions today and, with the Local Requirements country-expert mode, questions about a country's rules, citing the country record.
Answers are given in the user's language.
painPoints: Users who cannot find an answer quickly e-mail the specialists, which does not scale.
Answers not grounded in the record drift from what the platform enforces.

dependencies.name: R-AI Assistant (Onboarding and Country Expert)
dependencies.how: Answers the question from the knowledge base and country record.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Supplies the authoritative rule the answer cites.

steps.title: Escalate an unresolved question to a specialist
keyFacts: If R-AI cannot answer with confidence, the question becomes a task for the country specialist with the conversation attached.
Escalations are tracked with response times.
painPoints: Escalations by e-mail lose the context of what the user already tried.
Untracked questions are answered late or not at all.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Routes the question to the responsible specialist.

dependencies.name: R-AI Assistant (Onboarding and Country Expert)
dependencies.how: Attaches the conversation and context to the task.

steps.title: Answer and enrich the knowledge base
keyFacts: The specialist answers, and the answer is generalised into the country record or knowledge base so the next user gets it from R-AI.
Answers that reveal a gap in the record trigger a content update.
painPoints: Answers given one-to-one are repeated to every client.
Knowledge that lives in specialists' heads leaves with them.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Adds the clarified rule to the country record.

dependencies.name: R-AI Assistant (Onboarding and Country Expert)
dependencies.how: Publishes the answer for future questions.

steps.title: Track query resolution and response times
keyFacts: Query volumes, resolution times and topics per country are tracked, showing where the record or R-AI needs improvement.
Recurring questions are the roadmap for the country-expert mode.
painPoints: Without metrics, specialists are overloaded in silence.
Recurring questions are answered repeatedly instead of fixed once.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders
dependencies.how: Reports resolution times and volumes.

dependencies.name: R-AI Assistant (Onboarding and Country Expert)
dependencies.how: Reports which questions R-AI could not answer.

steps.title: Review country coverage currency periodically
keyFacts: Every rule set carries a last-reviewed date; records not reviewed within the target period are listed for review, prioritised by client entities in the country.
The review confirms deadline rules ahead of the next cycle's scoping.
painPoints: Countries without clients are neglected until a client expands there.
Rules that were never wrong are assumed still right.

dependencies.name: Country Regulations, Local Requirements and Local Forms
dependencies.how: Lists records due for review.

dependencies.how: Confirms deadline rules ahead of scoping.

outcomes: Financial and transactional data flows from the ERP into the model on schedule, with Excel as the fallback for entities outside the integration
Users log in through the group's identity provider with profiles that limit them to their own entities and roles
Integrations run under the platform's ISO 27001 controls with audit trails the client's IT security team accepts

steps.title: Assess integration options per ERP instance

Groups with several ERPs typically integrate the main instance and keep Excel for the rest.
painPoints: Integration projects that try to cover every ERP at once never finish.
IT departments asked for an integration without a data specification say no.

Mapping is versioned so extracts can be reproduced.

Unversioned mappings make historical extracts unreproducible.

The client's IT security review is supported with the platform's security documentation.

Security reviews without documentation stall the project for months.

rootGroups.name: Service Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a fixed-rate engagement to delivered documentation and back: how Reptune's specialists operate the same platform for Full Service and Collaborative clients and how clients switch service levels without rework.

streams.name: Deliver documentation as a service
streams.description: Run the Full Service and Collaborative service levels on the same platform the client licenses: engage at a fixed rate per Local File, collect data from the client, let Reptune specialists process, draft, localise and translate in a fraction of the time of traditional advisers while the client monitors progress on the dashboard, deliver the final files, use the included expert hours and let clients switch between On Demand, Collaborative and Full Service without rework.
outcomes: Full Service clients receive complete, compliant documentation at a known fixed fee per Local File and see progress at any time
Reptune specialists deliver each Local File in a fraction of the time of traditional advisers because the platform does the assembly
Clients move between service levels when their team changes, with the model, data and history carried over untouched

flows.title: Deliver Full Service Local Files at a Fixed Rate
flows.description: Engage and scope at a fixed rate per Local File, collect data from the client, process and draft, localise and translate, let the client review on the progress dashboard and deliver finals while recording hours.
flows.trigger: A client signs a Full Service engagement for the fiscal year, or a Collaborative client hands specific Local Files to Reptune.
flows.successSignal: All engaged Local Files are delivered final before their deadlines at the agreed fixed rate, the client has followed progress on the dashboard and included expert hours are accounted for.

steps.title: Engage and scope the engagement at a fixed rate per Local File
keyFacts: The engagement lists the entities and countries, the service level per item and the fixed rate per Local File, so the client knows the fee before the work starts.
Scoping uses the client's own cycle in the platform, so service items and client-led items sit in the same plan.
painPoints: Hourly adviser fees make documentation budgets unpredictable and cause groups to under-document.
Engagements scoped outside the platform drift from the client's actual scope.

dependencies.name: Documentation Scoping

steps.title: Collect data from the client's local contacts
keyFacts: The specialist issues data request tasks to the client's local contacts with prefilled templates, and chases through the platform's reminders rather than personal e-mail.
The client's coordinator sees which entities have delivered data and which are late.
painPoints: Data collection is the slowest part of any outsourced documentation project.
Specialists chasing data by e-mail lose margin on every file.

dependencies.name: Task Assignment, Collaboration and Reminders

dependencies.name: Full Service Delivery Workspace

Specialists prepare documentation in about 25 percent of the time of traditional advisers on this basis.
painPoints: Advisers who assemble documents in Word spend most of their hours on formatting.
Drafts prepared outside the client's platform cannot be maintained by the client later.

painPoints: Translation costs invoiced separately by advisers surprise the client.
Local advisers engaged per country deliver inconsistent files.

Advice given informally is neither recorded nor billed.
